title: macOS libkrun: a published port accepts connections but never forwards them, while the container answers inside the VM
body:
### Issue Description

On Podman machine with libkrun on macOS, a container port published on `127.0.0.1` sometimes stops forwarding. New TCP connections to the host port are accepted, but no bytes ever reach the container and nothing comes back, for at least 60 s. Every connection opened in that window behaves the same way, not just the first.

During the same seconds, another container on the same network connects to the published container's IP and port and gets an answer immediately, so the process behind the port is listening and serving. The container is `running` with exit code 0.

We see it while other containers and networks are being created and removed on the same machine at the same time. Starting the same container 100 times in a row, with nothing else going on, never reproduced it.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

We have no minimal reproducer yet. It reproduces within a few minutes with [gcpemu](https://github.com/linuxuser586/gcpemu)'s Host attachment tests. Those start several containers in parallel, each publishing one port with `HostIP: 127.0.0.1` (no fixed host port), and connect to it from the host straight after the container starts:

```sh
DOCKER_CONTEXT=podman go test -run '^(TestHostAttachmentOffers|TestHostAttachmentSurvivesRestart|TestOfferHeldOnWildcard)$' -count=10 -failfast -v ./services/compute
```

### Describe the results you received

The host saw this (each "ping" is a new TCP connection plus a request, abandoned after 5 s without a reply):

```
control port 127.0.0.1:45157 did not answer (relay container running, exit code 0): 12 pings failed, the last with: context deadline exceeded
a probe on <network> got the agent's answer at 10.89.0.254:7171
```

The second line is from a container on the same network, which connected to `10.89.0.254:7171` directly and got an answer.

### Describe the results you expected

Connections to the published port reach the container, as they do when the forward isn't stalled (the same start usually answers within about 100 ms).

- `podman-machine-default`: libkrun, 5 CPUs, 8 GiB memory
- Connections are made through the Docker-compatible API socket (`DOCKER_CONTEXT=podman`)

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged (the machine runs rootful: `rootless: false`)

### Additional environment details

The issue isn't caused by extra loopback aliases on the host (ruled out), by `DOCKER_HOST` vs. a docker context, or by the client.
